title: Per-field settings on an annotation are ignored for typed dictionaries and named tuples
text_original: Customizing un/structuring of _attrs_ classes, dataclasses, TypedDicts and dict NamedTuples is now possible by using `Annotated[T, override()]` on fields. See https://catt.rs/en/stable/customizing.html#using-typing-annotated-t-override for more details.
text_rewritten: Not every model in our codebase is a class. The layer that talks to the payment gateway is built out of typed dictionaries, and our geometry helpers are named tuples that we convert as dictionaries using the dict-shaped named-tuple hook factories. Those need exactly the same per-field settings our classes need: one key has to be sent as `from`, another must never leave the process. The existing per-field settings object, `cattrs.override(...)`, attached to the field's own annotation as `Annotated[T, override(...)]`, should be picked up automatically for these two shapes as well, in both directions and with no registration step beyond the named-tuple factories we already register. Fields with no such annotation must keep their own names.

The existing per-field settings object, `cattrs.override(...)`, attached to the field's own annotation as `Annotated[T, override(...)]`, should be picked up automatically for these two shapes as well, in both directions and with no registration step beyond the named-tuple factories we already register. acceptance_hint: A field annotated `Annotated[T, override(...)]` in a typed dictionary or in a dict-shaped named tuple is renamed or omitted by any converter in both directions, while unannotated fields keep their names.
